person.name: Alan_Turing
person.summary: Alan Turing was an English mathematician and pioneering computer scientist whose 1936 formulation of the Turing machine shaped theoretical computer science. During World War II he led key cryptanalytic work at Bletchley Park, and later designed early stored-program computer architectures and published influential papers on artificial intelligence and morphogenesis.

events.description: Alan Mathison Turing was born in Maida Vale, London, to Julius Mathison Turing and Ethel Sara Turing.

events.title: Determined journey to Sherborne School
events.description: On the first day of term during the General Strike, Turing cycled unaccompanied about 60 miles from Southampton to begin at Sherborne School.

events.title: Death of Christopher Morcom
events.description: Turing’s close friend and fellow student Christopher Morcom died, an event that profoundly influenced Turing and deepened his commitment to scientific study.

events.date_note: Undergraduate studies at King's College ran from February 1931 to November 1934

events.description: Turing started the mathematics course at King's College, later earning first-class honours.

events.title: Publishes 'On Computable Numbers'
events.description: The first part of Turing’s landmark paper 'On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem' appeared in the Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society, defining the Turing machine model.

events.title: Joins Bletchley Park codebreaking effort
events.description: Turing reported to the Government Code and Cypher School at Bletchley Park, later leading Hut 8 and devising methods (including improvements to the Polish bomba and Banburismus) to break German naval Enigma.

events.description: Turing travelled to the United States to collaborate with American counterparts on cryptanalytic techniques and machine design.

events.date_note: Joined the National Physical Laboratory in 1945; exact month not specified
events.title: Joins NPL to design the Automatic Computing Engine (ACE)
events.description: After the war, Turing moved to the National Physical Laboratory, where he initiated one of the earliest detailed designs for a stored-program computer, the ACE.

events.title: Appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE)
events.description: Turing was appointed OBE by King George VI for his wartime services in cryptanalysis.

events.title: Joins the University of Manchester Computing Machine Laboratory
events.description: Turing joined Max Newman’s laboratory, contributing to the development of early Manchester computers and pursuing research in computing and mathematical biology.

events.title: Publishes 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'
events.description: Turing’s Mind paper posed the question 'Can machines think?' and introduced the imitation game (now known as the Turing test) as a criterion for machine intelligence.

events.title: Convicted for homosexual acts; accepts hormone treatment
events.description: Turing was convicted of 'gross indecency' in Manchester and accepted hormone treatment (chemical castration) as an alternative to imprisonment.

events.date_note: Published in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B in 1952
events.title: Publishes 'The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'
events.description: Turing published a foundational paper in mathematical biology explaining pattern formation via reaction–diffusion systems, anticipating oscillating chemical reactions later observed experimentally.

events.title: Death in Wilmslow
events.description: Turing died from cyanide poisoning at his home in Wilmslow. An inquest ruled the death a suicide, though some evidence is consistent with accidental poisoning.
